key_facts: On Oct. 13, 2023, Best Buy emailed that it had received Plaintiff's application for General Warehouse Worker / 2nd Shift at $22.60, requisition 928556BR. The warehouse is 6653 Hopkins Road, Tracy, CA 95377. On Oct. 17 at 3:47 p.m., Jose Tapia, General Manager, emailed a congratulations offer for that job and required, within 24 hours, Candidate Zone signature, background-check information, and background-check authorization; California disclosure PDFs were attached but are not in this upload. At 4:22 p.m. Best Buy sent a background-authorization confirmation naming First Advantage Consumer Center. At 4:30 p.m. First Advantage ordered a Best Buy drug test (Q09078711; account BEST BUY 11759586; Quest Modesto listed as a collection option, not the worksite). Plaintiff accepted the offer and completed the drug screening. On information and belief, that screen came back clean. Best Buy then ceased communication and ghosted him. At 5:31 p.m. Best Buy HR had written 'Congratulations on accepting your offer' — that sentence is their characterization; Plaintiff independently accepted. No pre-adverse letter, adverse letter, or drug-test result PDF is in the file. The complaint does not attach a Best Buy report and does not allege its contents as a known fact. The load-bearing theory is information-and-belief use of § 290.46 disclosures. Supporting inference: written offer, same-day First Advantage screen, contemporaneous registry listing, and First Advantage's July 2024 UPS report matching this Plaintiff to the California registry — same vendor, same Plaintiff, methodology and matchability, not Best Buy transmission. Civ. Code §§ 1786.10 / 1786.22 inspection has not yet been demanded.
procedural_status: Executed verified complaint and San Joaquin intake dated September 8, 2026; signed, not yet filed. Plaintiff accepted the Oct. 17 offer, completed the drug screen (I&B clean), and was ghosted at 6653 Hopkins Road, Tracy. First Advantage is not a named defendant. § 290 is the third count. Lerma cannot run on an unattached Best Buy report. Serve the current SOS agent, not a warehouse. Do not bury Serrato disclosures that day.
damages: The offer states $22.60/hour for General Warehouse Worker / 2nd Shift. It does not state weekly hours or a start date. Portfolio valuation is $0. Contingent statutory remedies if use is proven: Penal Code § 290.46(j)(4)(A) actual/treble with a $250 floor, fees, exemplary damages, or a civil penalty capped at $25,000; ICRAA § 1786.50 actual damages or $10,000, whichever is greater. Do not import UPS/Pilot numbers.
risk: Stronger paper than Home Depot: written offer, $22.60, requisition, accepted offer, completed drug screen (I&B clean), confirmed Tracy warehouse, and a named vendor that is not a defendant. Still no rejection letter and no Best Buy report. Lerma dismissed after the employer's report was in the record — a demurrer cannot replicate that analysis while Best Buy withholds the report. If production later shows court records and no California-registry source, the 290 count dies then; ICRAA § 1786.40 can still reach discovery. Best Buy will move to compel arbitration based on the application-email recital; that is a defense, not a claim. Diversity removal is likely. Modesto is a collection-site option, not the worksite.
